title: Recording with Jelly Roll Morton in 1929
summary: Bigard recorded with anyone who wanted him and paid him, including Jelly Roll in 1929 while with Duke.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: See, that's a pretty good thing that he sent me that. They got things on there I never knew I made.

Do you remember any -- Let's see, I'm looking to see. Here's -- 1929 you recorded with Jelly Roll again, 'Smile the Blues Away,' "Turtle Twist," "In My Little Home" Dixieband, and "That's Like It Ought to Be", on RCA.
And that would be -- How did you happen to be recording with Jelly Roll, (Unintelligible) at the same time you were doing a lot of things with Duke, right?
I recorded with anybody who wanted to and wanted to pay me at that time. It didn't make any difference.
